title: POC Weekly Security Sync - Lakeside Health
summary: Weekly POC sync focused on security and compliance items during the pilot: SSO integration troubleshooting with Okta, audit log export and retention options, SOC 2 scoping and evidence sharing, encryption/KMS options, RBAC auditing, and concrete next steps for pilot sign-off. Action owners assigned for SOC2 documents, Okta config, sample audit log export, and retention confirmation.
next_steps: Redwood to share SOC2 scoping doc and certificate snapshot (Jordan) - eta 2025-11-07
Lakeside to confirm required retention window and any eDiscovery holds (Sara) - eta 2025-11-10
Jordan to provide sample audit log export and schema (shared drive) - eta 2025-11-06
Maya to send updated pilot pricing + dedicated capacity guidance - eta 2025-11-09
Schedule SSO deep dive with Lakeside DevOps for Okta config (Tom/Jordan) - week of 2025-11-10
action_items: Jordan: Upload SOC2 evidence index (partial) to shared drive by 2025-11-07
Tom: Provide exact retention requirement (in days) and any eDiscovery hold needs by 2025-11-10
Maya: Share pilot usage report and cost-to-date detail by 2025-11-06
Priya: Confirm stakeholder list for final security review by 2025-11-08
meeting_header: Date: 2025-11-04 | Start: 14:00 UTC | Duration: 38 minutes | Location: Zoom | Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Jordan Lee (Redwood SE), Sara Gomez (Lakeside CISO), Tom Reynolds (Lakeside Lead DevOps), Priya Nair (Lakeside PM)
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Patel: ok everyone good afternoon, thanks for joining our weekly POC security sync. quick roll call?
[00:06] Sara Gomez: Sara here, hi.
[00:08] Tom Reynolds: Tom on the call.
[00:10] Priya Nair: Priya here.
[00:12] Jordan Lee: Jordan from Redwood.
[00:14] Maya Patel: great. agenda is SSO updates, audit logs/retention, SOC2 evidence, and open risks. we'll go through current items and assign owners.
[00:28] Sara Gomez: sounds good. Tom and I had a follow-up from last week around SSO - we tried your test SAML metadata but saw assertion errors when we hit the staging endpoint.
[00:36] Jordan Lee: yeah i saw that in the staging logs, looks like the audience field was being set to the internal hostname, we pushed a config that should normalize the audience to the entityID used by your Okta app, but i want to walk through your Okta settings because sometimes they autofill the wrong value.
[00:50] Tom Reynolds: ok that matches what we saw. our IdP had two apps, one old and one new, some of the metadata got copied. i'll clean that up but can you share the exact entityID you expect? i think the doc link you sent has it but the testers were using a shorthand.
[01:05] Jordan Lee: sure, i'll put the exact entityID in the shared note after this call. probably the mismatch is what's causing the assertion/audience reject. also note that our staging runs on a host with a slightly different SAML endpoint so that tripped one of our customers too, it's a known caveat.
[01:20] Priya Nair: good to know. From compliance side Sara asked about SSO logging - we need to know how long those auth logs are retained and whether they are exported to our SIEM.
[01:30] Sara Gomez: yes, retention is critical. for PHI-adjacent access we need at least 365 days, and legal may request longer. also we need proof of admin actions in the UI.
[01:40] Jordan Lee: currently Redwood's hosted audit logs are retained 90 days by default in the pilot, but we do have options. Dedicated and Private deployments can extend retention to 365/730/indefinite with additional storage fee. we can also configure a log export to your S3 or push to your SIEM via webhook or syslog adapter.
[01:58] Tom Reynolds: can you do an export today for us, even a sample dump? we want to validate fields.
[02:04] Jordan Lee: yes i can generate a sample audit log export and drop it into the shared drive. it will include timestamps, actor, action, resource, request_id, and IPs. note there are some PII redaction switches - we can include or strip user emails per your policy.
[02:19] Sara Gomez: perfect. for SOC 2, where are you in certification? we need the report or at least scope evidence.
[02:26] Maya Patel: Redwood maintains SOC 2 Type II for the platform; Jordan has a scoping doc and a snapshot of the certificate we can share. we won't share full reports until NDA but we can provide the standard SOC 2 summary and control matrix for review.
[02:38] Jordan Lee: i'll put the SOC2 summary and the controls index in the drive; that'll show control owners, last audit date, and what evidence is available. some evidence is only available for Dedicated customers in certain cases, but most infra controls are covered for hosted.
[02:51] Priya Nair: does that include encryption at rest keys? we need to know if customer-managed KMS is available.
[02:58] Jordan Lee: for hosted we encrypt at rest with provider-managed keys, but we support CMEK (customer-managed encryption keys) for Dedicated and Private. for the pilot we can show envelope encryption details and provide attestations.
[03:12] Sara Gomez: ok. also need RBAC details - can we see admin audit trails for changes to RBAC roles and permission grants?
[03:20] Jordan Lee: yes audit logs include role changes and admin actions; we tag admin events explicitly. the UI shows an admin audit timeline and we can expose the raw logs via export or api.
[03:31] Tom Reynolds: one more - data residency. our legal team insists on us keeping production data in us-east-1 only. is that doable in the pilot?
[03:39] Maya Patel: hosted Redwood supports region pinning for accounts; your pilot org is currently in us-east-1 but we need formal confirmation. Dedicated and Private obviously allow for on-prem or region-limited infra.
[03:49] Priya Nair: we'll confirm but assume yes.
[03:52] Jordan Lee: quick note on telemetry - our runtime collects performance metrics and kv cache metrics, sometimes transcripts have partial mis-transcribes; we can separate business content vs telemetry logs.
[04:05] Sara Gomez: is there any risk that transcripts or user inputs, PHI, will leak to logs or used for model training?
[04:12] Jordan Lee: no training on customer data for hosted; we have a strict policy against using customer content for training. logs used for debugging are access-controlled and redacted as agreed. for more strict needs Dedicated/Private supports full isolation and CMEK.
[04:30] Maya Patel: noted. regarding eDiscovery and legal holds, we can support preserves via log export to your S3 and we can tag records with customer IDs to make retrieval straightforward.
[04:42] Sara Gomez: ok that'll help. another ask from legal was admin separation of duties - they want RBAC that can prevent a single user from elevating themselves and hiding actions.
[04:52] Jordan Lee: we support role hierarchies and require MFA for admin actions; changes to admin roles require approval workflow for Dedicated/Private. hosted has an admin guardrail and we can enable two-person approval for critical changes as part of the pilot via a configuration.
[05:10] Tom Reynolds: great. any known gaps we should be worried about?
[05:14] Jordan Lee: one small caveat: in staging some SAML metadata edge cases surface (like we hit earlier). also export pipelines to SIEM are near-rt but occasionally have small delivery delays; for strict forensics we recommend pushing to your S3 as primary.
[05:30] Priya Nair: timeline check - what's the ETA for the SOC2 docs and the audit log sample?
[05:36] Jordan Lee: SOC2 summary and controls index by 2025-11-07; sample audit log export by 2025-11-06. i'll drop both in the shared drive and notify the thread.
[05:46] Maya Patel: i'll also send a short pilot usage and cost snapshot by 2025-11-06 and follow up on dedicated capacity pricing.
[05:54] Sara Gomez: thanks. can we schedule the Okta deep dive next week? Tom and I are available tuesday morning US eastern.
[06:00] Maya Patel: noted, i'll coordinate via calendar.
[06:04] Priya Nair: one last question - backups and retention for transcripts/utterances, are they covered by the same retention policy or different?
[06:12] Jordan Lee: transcript retention follows the same audit/data retention config; we can separate call transcripts from audit logs and apply different retention windows if you need. for PHI we recommend 365+ retention with stricter access controls.
[06:28] Sara Gomez: ok that helps. thanks everyone.
[06:31] Maya Patel: recap real quick: jordan will upload SOC2 summary + controls index and sample logs; tom will confirm retention days; maya will send cost snapshot; schedule okta deep dive. any objections?
[06:44] Tom Reynolds: none from me.
[06:46] Sara Gomez: good.
[06:48] Maya Patel: great, thanks all. we'll follow up in the shared drive and thread. meeting adjourned.
